given: a stock table on which the drop migration has already removed inventory_code, leaving location, batch_number, and serial_number
when: the paired down-migration is applied to roll the change back
then: inventory_code is present again on every stock row, reconstructed as a combined code from the canonical location plus the split-out batch_number and serial_number

independence.rationale: AC1 and AC2 cover the forward drop and row survival; a build could implement an irreversible drop with no working down path. This AC is the separately-breakable reversibility outcome — the down-migration reconstructs inventory_code from the surviving columns — and can fail (missing or wrong down path) while the forward drop passes, and vice versa.

architectural_notes: Infra-layer migration-reversibility contract (PI5), realized by the Alembic downgrade paired with the AC1/AC2 upgrade and owned by the migrations module. The downgrade re-adds inventory_code and backfills it by reconstructing the combined code from the canonical location plus batch_number/serial_number — no runtime service or repository code participates. Cross-cutting concern: R1 reversibility/rollout safety, defended by a real-branch integration test that applies upgrade-then-downgrade against the paired Lakebase branch and asserts inventory_code is restored on every row, never via a mocked schema.
